#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# RESOLVED BEFORE THE `cd`, so a path you typed means what it says. The body
# runs from `python/`, and a relative operand resolved AFTER that would have
# quietly meant `v12/python/<what you typed>`.
#
# ONLY WHAT WAS SUPPLIED. `realpath -m ""` is an error, and resolving the
# OPTIONAL distro unconditionally made `just bootstrap inputs.json` -- the
# form that installs nothing -- fail in the shell before Python ever ran.
# An empty operand is passed through untouched so the refusal comes from the
# helper, by name, as it does for every other missing selection.
INPUTS_HERE="/tmp/review-input.json"
if [[ -n "/tmp/review-input.json" ]]; then INPUTS_HERE="$(realpath -m "/tmp/review-input.json")"; fi
DISTRO_HERE="--no-repositories"
if [[ -n "--no-repositories" ]]; then DISTRO_HERE="$(realpath -m "--no-repositories")"; fi
# TWO OPERANDS, NOT THREE. OWNER-STANDALONE-INTERFACE-20260916.md: "Finish
# the agreed two-argument bootstrap: it creates the bundled distro, databases
# and independent repositories." Naming a DISTRO is a development
# convenience; installing without one BUILDS the distribution here, so the
# owner never has to know where a build lands.
if [[ -n "/tmp/review-destination" && -z "--no-repositories" ]]; then
	just --justfile "/home/sl/src/baton/v12/justfile" build
	DISTRO_HERE="$(dirname "/home/sl/src/baton/v12/justfile")/python/build/out/distro"
fi
cd "$(dirname "/home/sl/src/baton/v12/justfile")/python"
PREPARED="$(python3 -m tools.environment interpreter)"
INSTALLING=()
if [[ -n "/tmp/review-destination" ]]; then
	INSTALLING+=(--destination "/tmp/review-destination" --distro "$DISTRO_HERE")
fi
EXTRA=()
if [[ -n "" ]]; then read -r -a EXTRA <<< ""; fi
exec env PYTHONPATH=src:. "$PREPARED" -m tools.bootstrap --inputs "$INPUTS_HERE" "${INSTALLING[@]}" "${EXTRA[@]}"
